release.text: A release every 42 days (0.8 a month), and the longest gap was 47 days. Delivery to users is regular. Keep the cadence and shrink what goes in each release. Track the number of changes per release over the next quarter.

leadTime.text: A change is open for a median of 2.5 days, then waits another 38.5 days merged and not yet released. 94% of its journey is waiting for a release, so faster review would barely move the 42.2 day median. Cut the wait, not the review: release smaller and more often, or let finished fixes out between trains. Compare the merged-to-released median after one quarter.

failure.text: 4 of 9 releases (44%) were followed by a Blocker or Critical bug within 30 days. That is a high change failure rate. Take the bugs listed below and trace what each release had in common (size, timing, a skipped check). Add one gate for the commonest cause and compare over the next four releases.

restore.text: Fixes for those serious bugs reached users a median of 35.9 days after the bug was raised, and the slowest took 42.9 days (85th percentile). The fix usually exists sooner than it ships. Allow an out-of-cycle patch release for any Blocker, and measure raised-to-released for the next three.
